react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of the ten differentially abundant metabolites reveals a dominant, highly consistent signal centred on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. Three complementary methods—RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity—converge on the same biological theme with no conflicting winners. The RaMP ORA (FDR ≈ 10⁻¹⁵) identifies KEGG:hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' (rank 0), WikiPathways WP:WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis' (rank 0), Reactome R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (rank 7), and SMPDB SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (rank 4) as the top hits, all sharing the same five steroid driver metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returns KEGG:hsa00140 as its sole significant hit, confirming the steroid cluster with the identical five compounds (dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁴) independently surfaces MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top-ranked pathway, again with perfect overlap of the same five steroids plus 7 α-hydroxy-DHEA as an inferred adjacent member. The 100 % concordance across ORA and network-diffusion paradigms constitutes a robust, multi-method consensus. The non-steroid compounds (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) are metabolically peripheral to this cluster; coumarin appears in a weak MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism hit (p = 0.045) that does not replicate in ORA tools and likely represents a secondary or noise-level association. The five steroid driver metabolites cover the full C19-androgen and C18-estrogen cores of the pathway, implying broad disruption of the CYP17A1/CYP19A1 axis rather than a single enzyme blockade. Spironolactone, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist present in the input list, may itself act as a steroidogenesis perturbant in the treatment group, explaining why the androgen/estrogen metabolome is globally altered.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of the ten differentially abundant metabolites reveals a dominant, highly consistent signal centred on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. Three complementary methods—RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity—converge on the same biological theme with no conflicting winners. The RaMP ORA (FDR ≈ 10⁻¹⁵) identifies KEGG:hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' (rank 0), WikiPathways WP:WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis' (rank 0), Reactome R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (rank 7), and SMPDB SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (rank 4) as the top hits, all sharing the same five steroid driver metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returns KEGG:hsa00140 as its sole significant hit, confirming the steroid cluster with the identical five compounds (dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁴) independently surfaces MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top-ranked pathway, again with perfect overlap of the same five steroids plus 7 α-hydroxy-DHEA as an inferred adjacent member. The 100 % concordance across ORA and network-diffusion paradigms constitutes a robust, multi-method consensus. The non-steroid compounds (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) are metabolically peripheral to this cluster; coumarin appears in a weak MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism hit (p = 0.045) that does not replicate in ORA tools and likely represents a secondary or noise-level association. The five steroid driver metabolites cover the full C19-androgen and C18-estrogen cores of the pathway, implying broad disruption of the CYP17A1/CYP19A1 axis rather than a single enzyme blockade. Spironolactone, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist present in the input list, may itself act as a steroidogenesis perturbant in the treatment group, explaining why the androgen/estrogen metabolome is globally altered.
